chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, it is the wergild (blood money).

key_terms.الْأَعْوَرِ: the one-eyed person (blind in one eye)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for injuring the eye of a person who is already blind in the other eye?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the loss of the remaining functional eye in an 'awar' (one-eyed person) constitutes a complete loss of sight, thereby warranting the full blood money (diyah) rather than a partial amount. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding how physical impairment is quantified in compensation, distinguishing between the loss of a specific organ and the loss of its primary function. It reflects the Imams' precise legal reasoning in applying general principles of injury compensation to specific physiological conditions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘With regards to an eye of the one-eyed, is the (complete) wergild’.
